utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Judge Morrison cannot be with us today due to an authorised Tribunal business. He will be back tomorrow. So we'll be sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We left off yesterday at Marin Dvor incident because it's important. Is this where the well-known Sniper Alley was?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what I've seen on television at the time, it's about in that vicinity, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with Unioninvest building and the so-called red building? Perhaps you have you've come across them from -- in UNPROFOR reports.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So no one every told you that you should check whether fire was opened from the red building or the Unioninvest building; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 65 ter 21216. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise this photo, Mr. Van der Weijden? You can; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the buildings on the photo, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that between the buildings of the museum and philosophy school the street that runs between them is the Franjo Racki Street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know the name of the street, but that is the street that I've marked as the field of fire in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark it again. Draw a line from the Metalka building all the way to the tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know the Metalka building, exactly which building that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What building, then, did you mark as the possible site where the origin of fire was?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please draw a line all the way to the tracks beginning with that -- from that building.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you see the street to the left of the School of Philosophy? At the time it was called Djure Danicica Street, and today I believe it's called Ferde Hauptmana Street or Kosta Hermana Street.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see a street left of the faculty, parallel to the street that I've just marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please draw a line or mark that street from the red building to the tracks, running down that street. Can you see that head building beyond Metalka building? It's approximately in line with Djure Danicica Street.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this building?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That building and the next one, the one next to it.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now please draw a line from those buildings to the tram tracks running down Djuro Danicic Street.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Van der Weijden, were you informed under whose control these red buildings were?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please date and initial this photo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to point out that this photo is, again, in perspective and that from street level these buildings would be blocked from view from the tram lines by this group of buildings down below.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, the testimony of an UNPROFOR observer in the Milosevic case, of witness Asam Butt is not to that effect. He said that the red buildings were dominant, that they were higher. Now, have you ever checked these buildings? Did you ever go there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not check the buildings because from the location of the incident site I could not see those buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: These are all waste of time, Mr. Karadzic. The witness does not know anything. But we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, before we do so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I request that the witness mark on the diagram the buildings which prevent a direct line of sight, which he's just indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about putting the numbers? Mr. Tieger, do you have anything to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Only to indicate that I think the witness did indicate that with the circle; it's just that the record would not have reflected what that last circle meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, so why don't we put to the rectangular -- number 1 for that rectangular building, and what do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the building that I believe has been used as the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Origin of fire. And the red building --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The red buildings I will mark with 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- number 2. And number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 3 is the group of building that would prevent the line of fire [sic] from the red buildings to the tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Defence Exhibit ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D649.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, how do you know that building number 3 obstructs the view from building number 2?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I also checked this street and I did not see the buildings, the red buildings, beyond, when I visited the -- that neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Can we -- can we have those markings again, please? We've lost them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll bring back the -- D649.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 21215 from the same binder, the photo preceding the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like now to ask you to do the same thing we've done earlier, to show the building that you assume was under Serb control and then also on Rasko Street from the red building down the street to the tram tracks. So, in other words, could you please mark both streets from both of those buildings down all the way to the tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've not marked in my report anywhere where a building is under Serb control. I've only marked buildings of -- marked buildings that I believe as the origin of fire. I did not indicate any party. But this building is where I believe the shooter has fired from, down this street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's put number 1 for that building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please circle the two red buildings.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mark it to indicate that it's number 2, and then draw a line towards the track down Djure Danicica Street.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you see to the right of this the white, square building some five to six storeys high?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Could you please put a number 3 there.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Has anyone informed you that that was the Unioninvest building, which was also under Muslim control?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you now please draw the line of vision from the western corner of this building towards the tracks.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: For -- to draw a line of vision, I would have to visit the site and look at street level, but for a line from this -- from the left corner to the tracks, I will just draw this. So this is, in my view, not the line of vision, but it's just a line to the tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that on the other side of the bridge, from Vrbanja bridge, the street that leads on is called Trscanska Street. Can you see the bridge?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see a bridge on the right side of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that Branimira Cosica Street runs from it and then on, after the high-rise, Trscanska Street continues towards the hospital?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know the name of the streets at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Would you please date and initial this photo.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D650.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can now remove this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, do you remember the Dragomir Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that case, did you work on this incident as well as on the incident in which Alma Cehajic was wounded?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to view the report, they match.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I then relate you to the first instance judgement in the Dragomir Milosevic case. This is an incident that occurred on the 8th of October involving Alma Cehajic, and Mulaosmanovic came to testify here. And we will find this on pages 84 and onward. Mr. Van der Weijden, you testified and produced an expert report on -- for many cases before this Tribunal, and these two incidents were part of your reports. Now, do you recall that you mentioned certain matters and there, for instance, in paragraph 303 where you said that the tram --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For record, what's the date of the incident in which Mulaosmanovic was injured? Is it not F15 incident, 27 February 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was on the 27th of February. And the paragraph that relates to that is paragraphs 300 and higher. So could we please look now at paragraph 300 where says --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this first, Mr. Van der Weijden: Have you updated your findings to reflect the adjudicated facts?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have reviewed all cases, but I would have to look at the report, the previous report, to check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I will try to assist you now. And I'd like to refer you to paragraph 300 of the first instance judgement in the Milosevic case. That's on page 100. And in the paragraph it says: "In one UNPROFOR report of the same day, which was shown by the Defence, it is stated that the tram which was near the Holiday Inn had been shot by eight shots in which incident one person was wounded, and it's possible that three other individuals were wounded or killed. In the same report, it says that these bullets were fired in the Vrbanja Most region and the red building area where at the time there was fighting and shooting between the SRK and the BH Army." And that's in footnote 1.062 from a report, an UNPROFOR report sitrep, of February, pages 2 to 9. And then a few pages on, it says that military observers of the UN conducted an investigation into the alleged incident and confirmed that the tram was hit by -- with eight bullets and that the fire had been opened from the south. And then Witness W-118 explained that that report probably did not refer to the incident when her tram had been hit, because in the report mention is made of an exchange of fire between the two sides, and Alma Mulaosmanovic could not confirm that there was any shooting at the time when the tram had been hit. In addition, the report also mentions that the tram was close to the Holiday Inn, which, according to Witness W-118, was an area near Marin Dvor, Holiday Inn, and not the area near the Marsal Tito Barracks where the tram had been. Now, in the report, in the UNPROFOR report, the red buildings is mentioned as the building from which fire was opened; and according to Witness 118, that area is not the same as the Grbavica area which she had talked about, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have the original text that was read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the last sentence, the area of the Vrbanja bridge-red building, which was mentioned in the UNPROFOR report as the place from which the fire was -- fire was opened, is not the same area as the Grbavica area. Now, would you agree with me that this is in fact the same area because these two buildings are one next to the other?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not read from your statement that the Vrbanja Most area and the red building area is the same as the red building or the bridge. It's an area, so it might be -- I don't know how big that area is, mentioned in the UNPROFOR document. So they might include the buildings that I think the fire came from. But I only see, as you've read from the UNPROFOR report, an area instead of specific buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, in your analysis, would you have paid more attention to UNPROFOR reports because they observe the developments throughout the day rather than opinions that people who are on the tram were willing to -- to provide?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've stated yesterday, my method was, with the brief situation description, to go to a location, view the incident site, and in my view determine the origin of fire. If some of the -- my findings correspond with UNPROFOR reports or witness reports, that is okay, but it doesn't influence my judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember -- let's look at paragraph 3.4 on page 101. Lieutenant Van der Weijden in his report also states that the sniper was probably on the Metalka building. However, the Trial Chamber has in mind that Lieutenant Van der Weijden thought that the tram was on the cross-roads between the museum and the Holiday Inn, farther to the east from the area where the tram, as witnesses have confirmed, had been hit. Witnesses W-118 and Alma Mulaosmanovic and Alija Konjak confirmed that the shot had been fired from one of the high-rises in Grbavica area. In other words, the people on the tram claim that they knew where the shot had come from. And your opinion is mentioned here as being of -- as being opposite to that. Now, would you please take a look at paragraph 106 of the judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, do you have the judgement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have the judgement before me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let him read it. But -- while I don't see any point of analysing the other Chamber's judgement at this moment, if you'd like to put a specific question, it is incumbent upon you to show that paragraph to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have a hard copy in the Serbian version, but I would like to discuss something that's very important for this case, and that is where the tram exactly was hit and the time when it occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Van der Weijden, do you know where the tram was at the moment when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Put your question, and you can submit your submission later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the tram was when it was hit? Were you able to establish that, or did anyone establish it and you accepted that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What incident are we talking about? F15 incident where Alma Mulaosmanovic was injured?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Incidents 11 and 15. First incident 11 and then 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In case of 11, according to the situation, the tram was approaching from the west to the east, the intersection between the Museum of the Revolution and the Faculty of Philosophy. So it was just in the direct vicinity of the crossing that fire was opened. And for case 15 -- just a moment. There it's only mentioned that the tram was near the Tito Barracks, which are close to the Holiday Inn and the same intersection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you bring back D650.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you say close to the Holiday Inn, does that mean before the intersection or after the intersection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, can you see those -- both those points in this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For case F11 -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can use the black one, if necessary. Could you wait a minute, or are you accustomed to that tool already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the two buttons, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's give it a try.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excellent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For case F11, it would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you just put F11 there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The tram was traveling from west to east and nearing the intersection which is this intersection between the museum and the faculty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the second incident.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second incident, I would have to go a little more to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we will do it again. We cannot keep this one. I will ask him to mark it again. No, no, we bring back 650 anew. Is it fine, Mr. Van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A little more to the left, please. No, all the way to the other side. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. So could you mark F11 again. Yes, we can do that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks] And for case F15, the tram is travelling from the Old Town, so it will be travelling westwards in the vicinity, but it doesn't give it distance because Tito Barracks is a large area, so it's -- these are the -- and more to the west. These are the Tito Barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Put the date and your signature, please, Mr. Van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D651.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, was it important for you to know where the tram was exactly when it was hit? What were the positions of the bodies that were hit? And how did the entry/exit wounds look like?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the first question, it would -- would be important for me to know exactly when it was hit. As for the second questions, I have not seen the positions of the bodies, nor have I seen the entry/exit wounds -- entry and exit wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that a thigh on a human body is below the hip?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if an entry wound is in the thigh and the exit wound is in the hip, the canal then stretches from down, upwards. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wound canal would stretch upwards, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 304 of the judgement, I'm going to read it out to you, it says the following: "Lieutenant Van der Weijden said in his report that the sniper was probably in the Metalka building. However, the Trial Chamber bore in mind the fact that the lieutenant thought that the tram was at the intersection which was much more to the east as shown by the eyewitnesses." Now, can you see these two streets and that Djure Danicica street is somewhat more to the east than the Djure Racko Street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say in my report that there was mention of a sniper, just to justify that. And -- which case? This is still case F11?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In case 11, there's -- I do believe that the location of the tram that I was given by the OTP was slightly different from the location where I believe the tram was at the time of the incident, but it's not far more to the east; it's only a little bit -- little bit maybe 50 metres further to the east, in front of the faculty building. So not the -- the next intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that between these two blue lines the distance is not more than 50 metres?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree or do you remember that it was concluded that on the Racki Street you think was the path of the bullet, then in that case the tram must have been approaching an S-curve and had to slow down?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. Mr. Karadzic is now putting questions to the witness as to the factual findings made by the Trial Chamber in the Dragomir Milosevic case with which the witness is not necessarily familiar. Mr. Karadzic should be putting factual assertions to the witness and ask him if he agrees or if he disagrees, or he can put the witness's prior evidence to him, or he can put items of evidence relied upon by the Trial Chamber in that case; but asking the witness whether he recollects a judgement that he hasn't necessarily read or asking him to engage in comparative factual analysis with that carried out by the Trial Chamber in that case is inappropriate in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. That's what I told him to do. Put a specific question as to his evidence or put your specific factual questions. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question, with all due respect to Mr. Gaynor, was relating to an enormous number of adjudicated facts, and the burden of disproving them is on my shoulders. Many of them stem from the Milosevic judgement. Mr. Van der Weijden testified in all these incidents, and it was established that the tram had to slow down on the Racki Street because it was approaching the S-curve. I'm asking Mr. Van der Weijden if he knew that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have on the ELMO this particular section of the map in order for us to determine where the right-hand tram track forks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have a 65 ter number of that map, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so. That's the map provided by the US government, and we have already seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you first please show this so that we can establish what this refers to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think ELMO is working at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm kindly asking for your patience, because you will realise how enormously important these facts are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it we should have a 65 ter number of what Mr. Van der Weijden is now looking at.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the OTP to have understanding, because we realised this overnight, and it seems that the previous Trial Chamber was misled by an incomplete presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a totally inappropriate comment, Mr. Karadzic. Now, yes, we have ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, do you agree that this is a picture taken from the Holiday Inn Hotel?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree it's a picture taken from the direction of the Holiday Inn but not from within the Holiday Inn at all. It's from an elevated position above. It's probably from a helicopter. But it's looking down at the curve in the tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this is this so-called Sniper Alley that features in many incidents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not visited Sniper Alley at that time. I only seen it on television, so I only know where the -- the wider area is. I do not know if this is the exact location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We shall nevertheless try to find this photograph in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it this is a magnified or zoomed-in picture of 21216. If we bring up Exhibit -- 65 ter 21216, but not marked, but we can recognise it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That's exactly right. Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit -- no, not exhibit. 65 ter 21216, map 7 of the binder. The bottom part.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you mark the Racki Street, Mr. Van der Weijden, which, according to you, coincided with the projectile trajectory, and also this S-curve.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be the street. I do not know the name that I've identified as the field of fire. And the S-curve for the -- in this incident from the tram travelling from --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden appears to be marking with the pen. It's not coming up on the version that I'm looking at. I don't think it's coming up, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Oh, thank you. I had the wrong picture. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please carry on, Mr. Van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this would be -- this stretch would be the S-curve.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Van der Weijden, for how long this S-curve had been existing? Did it exist at the time when the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any other different signs of construction for the dead-line or the lines in the centre, so I assumed that they were present at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put the date and your initials.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like this to be tendered into evidence. And after that I would appreciate to see the map provided by the US government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be exhibited as Defence Exhibit D652.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please ask the Registry to show us on the ELMO the publisher and the date of the map that we can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this map dates from 1993, and the bit below that you will see that it was published by the State Department? The name of the publisher must be a little bit towards the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the correct reference. There must be a publisher mentioned somewhere because there's no doubt that it was provided by the State Department of the US government. Yes, I think we can see it now. Thank you. Can I please now ask for the section that I have marked to be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Move it a little bit right, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, can I ask you now to identify the tram track and to mark the bifurcation place on the tram track, which means where it is forking into two directions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like the witness to mark on the original map? That's the only possible method at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe after the break, after we have made a copy. But I can give him the map of Sarajevo, although I'm sorry to see it used in this way, and then we can look at the US map later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Van der Weijden, that the right stretch of the tram deviates from the main track at the point where the church Marin Dvor on Trscanska Street is and which is far away from the area that was constructed after the year 2004?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see the transcript, please? Yes, I agree that on this city map, where the tram track splits, it's farther away from the intersection than I -- than this split at the intersection where I believe the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please put a circle around this particular location on the map where the split is between the two tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, can we not find the map which depicts this area from this Sarajevo booklet?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, we'll try and find it immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can just mark it here? [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will be easier if we get an e-court version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the Unioninvest building close to the Vrbanja bridge; and if you do, could you please mark it.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see the Wilson promenade opposite Grbavica? So the Wilson promenade.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recognise that name on the city map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is where the river ends -- or, rather, it's parallel to the river. So it's on the Muslim side, exactly across from Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about sheet 7 of that map binder, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would it be the same as Visanova Cetiliste [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, if you speak -- please speak to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Would that be Visanova Cetiliste?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But just a second. Let's wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could bring up 65 ter 09390C, that should represent -- give this part of Sarajevo. Page 13, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We should have page 13, which is 0546-6581.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, did you mean this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. The top -- the top left of that area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 13 would be better, which is 0546-6581. It's identical, but it's readable. So the page number is 0546-6581.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to point out that I think there is a mix-up in different split-ups, because as visible on page 88 of my paper report, of my expert report, I'm -- there's already visible the next intersection where the tram lines, also according to the map, split. But the split where I -- on the intersection where I believe the incident took place is just a split where the -- from whereon the tram lines run parallel to the same street and then further split up into different directions. And I'm sure if we would have a better photo from Google Earth it would be clearly visible that it's a different intersection that Mr. -- Mr. Karadzic is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Unless we can find the proper map to which both parties can agree, then we shall proceed with that map on the ELMO. I propose to take a break for 20 minutes. In the meantime, then I hope the parties can sort out all the maps. If it is agreeable.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break for 20 minutes. --- Break taken at 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. I see a map on our bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, would you now please mark the spot where the tram tracks fork, where they separate and then make a loop around the centre of town. Can we agree that this is near number 8, near the Vrbanja bridge and Trscanska Street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a split of tram tracks at location number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Van der Weijden, could you please tell us -- or can you confirm that you have actually been misled by the new situation with the tracks and that based on that you concluded that the tram was visible on the bullet path or within the scope of the trajectory of the bullet for eight seconds? Correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not correct. If I could have an aerial photograph of that area, I could point out how I came to my conclusions. Since there are two dividing -- two points within a short distance where the trams separate -- the tram lines separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I suggest it might be helpful if Mr. Van der Weijden could refer to his -- the aerial photographs in his report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are not detailed enough. I would need an aerial photograph of Sarajevo. And I believe there is somewhere, but it would have to be straight down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for the record, the map we are looking at is -- I take it is Exhibit D617, which we admitted through Dr. Nakas. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I understand that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to tender it through this witness to point out the fork in the tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, when was the photo taken that you have referred to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall on what date the Google Earth photo that I used for my report was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But would you agree with me that Google Earth did not exist at the time and that it is being updated every two or three months nowadays; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That might be. Could I, then, have the area which I marked 1 magnified, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could we have that magnified, but I will also show the American map, the US map, the 1993 map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can we just bear in mind the time periods. Up until 2004, was the fork in the tram tracks here at the spot which you marked next to number 8?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a fork at the location number 8, yes. But I do not know until 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like the map zoomed in any further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So could you mark the fork part again for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's good.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you use the pen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- Your Honour, would I be allowed to draw something on the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You will see that even from aerial photography that should be made at the time by NATO forces or any other, that if you would have a view of the tram tracks, you will see that there is a split up of tram tracks here. And since the tram tracks along the roads at the intersection number 8 - the northern one, it runs on the north side of the street and the southern one runs on the south side - there is a previous split up a little more to the west where I believe the intersection is where the incident happened. Just for planning purposes, because I think for planning -- for city planning this would be a more difficult situation. So if you would have an aerial photograph, you would see that there are two split-ups of the tram tracks. That's what I would like to point out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you put number 1 and 2 for those intersections and that split.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 1 is the first split, and number 2 is the split that's also visible on the city maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where does the right fork from the first intersection, the first split, where does that lead? Where does it go?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It runs parallel to -- on the same street, but only on the south side of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why can we not see it on any map before 2004? Mr. Van der Weijden, I lived in this city, and I know exactly where the tram forked and where it forks today. So why could we not find this fork before 2004 on any of the maps?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it's -- it's a map, and it doesn't necessarily show the exact -- the width of the line of the street does not also specifically mark the -- the width of the street. It's a map, and it's a guide to reality. And I believe since -- from that -- that S-curve that I describe at the intersection of the incident site, because the tram lines run parallel to the same street it's not mentioned in -- it's not shown on the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, I'll show you now a US map, and it's rather accurate. This is a US government map from 1993. And we also have a Muslim -- or, rather, a Sarajevo map of 2004. And we can see that the only fork was in line with Trscanska Street, which is now called Zavidovicka Street, or something like that, and that's at number 8. And you cannot locate this in any other map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I would like some assistance from the Court Usher to show the witness this map that we've already identified earlier. The Prosecutor has seen the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So could the witness now please mark on this map. And could we place it on the ELMO, please. So could the witness please mark this US map and show us where the fork in the tram tracks was. Would you please mark Trscanska Street. Can you see it? T-r-s-c-a-n-s-k-a. Perhaps if you can put the map up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then Branka Radicevica Street. That's below Hotel Zagreb. That street, too, has a new name now.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the place where the fork is, Mr. Van der Weijden, in line with the Catholic church that we can see there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is fork -- there is a fork at that intersection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the west of this fork we see that the track -- there's a double track; and to the east of it, the loop going around the centre, the Sarajevo city centre, is only one set of tracks; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see the transcript? This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, but what have you just marked now?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is -- on this map, there is a tram line with a loop that I marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But is this the only way you can take this -- these tracks, would be if you're going from the city centre to the railway station; correct? For us, this fork is irrelevant. Let me just repeat the question. To the west of the fork we see that there is a double track, and to the east we only see one set of tracks going south and north.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Can I ask you to submit this to Mr. Witness, this original. No, no, no. Not on the ELMO. On the ELMO it can be the copy. And just to help him see better.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the west of the crossing with the Catholic church there was only one track leading west, and then after approximately 150 metres there's another track with the loop splitting off to the north-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that that is the fork leading to the railway station and that it's irrelevant to this case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the black building with the multiple lines is the railway system -- station, it would be irrelevant, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you tell us, how do you mark on a map double tracks, and are -- these vertical bars, are they actually an indication that there is a track to the west of the fork?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not conclude that from the legend of this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But can we agree that before the fork that you've indicated there are no other forks? There is no fork on this map to the west of the fork that you identified and that the tram did not have to slow down at any point there because of some alleged S-curve.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that there is no other indication of a fork on this map. But it's not a fork, it's an S-curve.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, the curve actually exists at -- from the point where the tracks fork, and then -- and you have indicated that spot. Now, after the war, the fork was near the Holiday Inn, and the purpose was to make it -- to make the traffic flow more easily in this area, and the thing is that you have used the map that was of a later date and thus were misled. And, of course, I do not blame you or the Trial Chamber for it, but would you agree with me that this kind of reality set in after 2004 and that there are no indications whatsoever on earlier maps that there was a curve at the time of the events?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not know. I'm not aware of the city planning in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, very well, but I'm talking about documents here. Now, let me ask you this: Now, you have agreed that the hip on the human body is above a thigh. Now I would like to read paragraph 256 in the judgement, in the Milosevic judgement: "When the fire -- firing started, panic set in. People tried to hide behind seats. The shots first hit the upper portion of the tram and then the bottom part of the tram, and then the victim" - I don't want to mention the name - "was standing next to the central door, tram door, and was turned with her back to Grbavica. She was wounded in the left part of her head, and also a bullet ran through her right thigh, hitting and severing the large artery." Now, how would you explain the wound canal, that it was actually ascending, it was going from a lower angle to a higher angle if the shot was from a higher ground, from the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not from which place the entry wound exactly was because the right thigh is a large part of the leg, but the bullet also enters the tram and it can already deviate its -- its trajectory from just entering the tram. So I do not know from exactly which angle the bullet entered the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you know very well what a ricochet does to the body. It does not cause an entry/exit wound but, rather, a different kind of wound, and here it was established that the bullet had entered the thigh and exited it. But here it also says that Mr. Van der Weijden, in his report, concluded that "the shooter was probably on the roof of the Metalka building," and so on and so forth. Now, two questions: Mr. Van der Weijden, had you had a medical report showing that the entry wound was in the thigh and the exit wound near the hip, would your conclusions have been different?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not conclude that the shooter was on the roof of the Metalka building, since being on the roof is tactically not a very good position. And I did not have a medical report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Maybe it was a misinterpretation. It says here that the shooter -- it was concluded that the shooter was on the Metalka building. So that's one. But now, had you known what the situation was at the time of the incident, that there was no fork and no S-curve, would your conclusion have been different in terms of those eight seconds of visibility of the tram? Would it have been perhaps that it was only three seconds or so?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusion would be the same, but I agree that the eight seconds, if there was no S-curve at the time, the eight seconds would be less. It would probably be four seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please now initial the map, the hard copy map, please. Would you mark the fork and put your initials and date on the map, on the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the original?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the copy, please. I need the original.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Let us see the marking again. What does number 2 refer to, Mr. Van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be the incident site. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then just a second. For a better view, we'll admit the clean version as well to see the S-curve in the -- in number 1 area. So we will admit this marked map as Exhibit D -- what number should be given?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D653, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we'll admit, separately, a clean version of this map, another copy, as Exhibit D654.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. Now, would you agree with me that the direction of the origin of fire can be established on the basis of the bullet that is recovered? Now, would you agree with me that if a bullet hits soft ground that then it would not ricochet, and then if -- if it -- if the ground was harder it would ricochet and cause a cloud of dust?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's not for the witness. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yeah, indeed that point. And also my previous point, which is to request the accused to put each assertion in turn to the witness so the witness has an opportunity to respond to each assertion instead of building these compound questions with five or six in-built questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise, but I'm trying to save some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, would you agree with me that if a bullet -- the incoming angle of the bullet is small, then there would be a cloud of dust that would be almost horizontal, above the spot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be different for every -- every surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, if the ground is soft, dusty?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the ground is soft and dusty, there will be a larger cloud.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how would this cloud of dust disperse, for instance, if a bullet, the incoming -- the angle of incidence was, let's say, 20 degrees?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would depend on the wind conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what happens if there's no wind?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there's no wind, the dust will hang in the air until it drops back to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But it would move in any direction. The dust particles would also have certain angle of their own to indicate the direction from which the bullet came.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some conclusions could be drawn from the spread of the dust.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at the video footage V0000-000 -- 4374 from 3 minutes and 29 seconds onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this incident of the 8th of October was recorded live by the Sarajevo Television?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do not know that, but I assume that it's recorded live.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now play this video, which starts at 2 minutes -- 3 minutes 29 seconds until 3 minutes, 36 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please replay again. And can you please pay attention to the dust that was created by the burst of fire.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have 1D2418.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But before that, can you see the Franjo Racki Street, that is to say, the street that in your view coincides with the trajectory?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I not know where this video exactly was shot, so I do not know which street is intended.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the foreground is the Faculty of Philosophy and in the background is the museum?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the faculty. And the museum I cannot recognise. But it's -- that look -- exactly in the centre of the image, that looks to be the intersection from -- on which the curve, S-curve, is visible, by the way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have document 1D2418. It's a still photo or a photo of the same location. 1D2418.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the photograph. Do you agree or have you noticed that fire was opened at the people walking down the pavement and that two individuals remained lying on the ground? We can see these two people in this photo; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this photo, I do not see people lying on the ground. But in the video just shown, I did see people on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in respect to this location, Djuro Danicic Street is instead of Franjo Racki Street? To the east of the faculty, if you remember, was Djure Danicic Street; and to the west, between the faculty and the museum, was Franjo Racki Street; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that in this case the fire appears to be coming down -- down a street east of the street that I've indicated in my incidents -- or the incidents that I examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 65 ter 40374. It's a video footage. Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the two people falling down onto the ground?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I see three people, actually, falling to the ground. Two people are actually lying on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have document 1D02419. It's a photo. It's number 18. We need number 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, do you see this young boy in a jacket lying on the pavement and the other person being assisted by some people?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us now look where this boy in the green jacket was wounded, and for that we need 65 ter -- it's the same footage, but it starts at 06:26 until 06:38 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the boy in the green jacket that had been lying there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the gentleman who is carrying him and who is quite calmly smoking a cigarette or having it in his mouth and that he also has a radio, Motorola, in his breast pocket?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see something, but I don't know for sure that's something of a radio.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have photo 1D02-2420. It's another photo which is more accurate. So we need photo number 20. This one was number 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now see that he has a cigarette in his mouth and that there is a radio set with the antenna in the breast pocket of his shirt?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the cigarette, but I could not conclude that it's a radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It doesn't take too much imagination to conclude that this is, in fact, a radio. Do you agree that this person was wounded in his right leg, a little bit below the hip? Rather, both persons.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see a dark spot, but I could not see exactly where he was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to the bloodstain, would you say that this is the right leg below the hip?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this picture, I can see a dark spot, but I do not see the complete wound, so I -- I'm not going to draw any conclusions for where the wound exactly is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If the wound is -- is underneath this stain, would you say that it is approximately 70 centimetres from the ground?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably 70 to 80 centimetres, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have back 1D02419, please, so that we can see the position of this person on the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this boy in the green jacket was about one metre from the edge of the payment and that the man who is in front of him was also about one metre from the edge of the pavement? And would you agree that the boy in the green jacket was hit first and then this man was hit second?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not draw that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play back the video-clip 65 ter 40374.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can see where this boy's right leg is. Please pay attention at the moment when this boy in the green jacket falls down and when the other man falls down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the boy in the green jacket was the first to fall down?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you agree, then, that they were hit while they were one behind the other or one in front of the other?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look now at 1D02421.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this stain, this bloodstain, is visible in a better way and that it is located between the knee and the hip? This is the boy who was standing in front but was hit later, because he's wearing a blue jacket, not the green one.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that there is a bloodstain on the -- between the knee and the hip, on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this person is a little bit bulkier than the person in the green jacket and that he was wounded in the right leg approximately 70 centimetres from the ground?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- from the video, he appears to be older than the other -- than the man in the green jacket, and the height would be, again, in the 70 to 80 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look again the video from 3:29 to 3:36. Please pay attention to these two falling persons and to the dust going up next to them on the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's play it back again. Just look at how they're falling and how the dust is rising.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the photo 1D02423. 2423. I think that's the next one. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in the part that is being marked by this arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, do you agree that the dust is going vertically up under a large angle, probably 90 degrees or thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The particles are going up from the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, from the Serbian positions that were 321 metres away and at the elevation of 13 metres, the descent angle in this situation could be maximum 5 degrees?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did calculate that yesterday evening, and it would be just about 5 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Defence is grateful to you for taking your time to do that. We have seen on the footage that the dust is almost next to the edge of the pavement. Can we now assume that the shooter was very precise and that the element of shooting were almost identical. So if he failed to hit someone, the bullet would land right to the edge or the kerb at the pavement?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree, since I did hear multiple shots that would indicate a machine-gun, and a machine-gun is built to spread bullets and not to -- for all bullets to end up at the same location. So he might fire one shot in the grass and the other shots a little bit higher. It's a cone of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you can see where these people who are hit are. They are a metre away from the place where the dust is going up. What's the distance between their entry wound, which is 70 metres above the ground, and the edge of the pavement? It's approximately 90 degrees. I'm talking about angle. So, you see, they are not very far away from the pavement, and they were hit at about 70 or 80 centimetres above the ground. Can that make a 5 degree angle or a 35 or 45 degree angle?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was just one bullet, it would not be possible. Or it would be very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Each of them was hit with one bullet only.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can all the photographs and the video-clip that we showed be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will deal with them one by one. First we deal with the video footage. We saw two parts of that video, 65 ter number 403 was 374. First part is from 3 minutes, 28 seconds and on. They will be given a separate number first. That will be Exhibit D655.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then second part of that video which ran from 06 minutes, 38 seconds, that will be given Exhibit D656. And then we saw five pictures, stills of that -- of those video footage. If first, 1D2418 will be given Exhibit D657. 2419, Exhibit D658. 1D2420 will be given the number of Exhibit D659. 21, D660. And 23 be given the number of D661. I think we dealt with everything. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall incident number 7 from Schedule F that took place on the 25th of May, 1994?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which documents did you have at your disposal when you were working on this case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those would be the documents listed on page 57 of the paper copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you establish the location of the bus at the -- at the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location of the bus was shown to me by the investigator, together with GPS coordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then on the basis of this -- but first tell me who showed this to you. Was that an OTP investigator or a Bosnian investigator?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OTP investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then on the basis of this information and the location indicated to you, what did you establish?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shown the location and the orientation of the bus, that the bus was standing with its nose oriented south/south-west, exposing the right side, down the street, to the north-west. From those, together with the witness statements, I concluded that the shot must have originated from down that street and that it was a single bullet since there was -- in the witness statement there's only a single bullet mentioned. It would be easy to find other bullets since it would have entered the side of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In which particular part did the bullet penetrate the bus?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen it. I've only had the witness statements -- the witness statements at my disposal for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have any expert report -- or, rather, forensic and criminal investigation report about the bus provided by the Sarajevo authorities?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But was it necessary -- in view of all these elements that you had, wouldn't it have been necessary for you to know, in view of orientation of the bus, the place where the bus would be entered, and would that indicate the origin of fire and the place from which the shot originated?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be helpful but not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So why, then, did you accept the suggestion that the shot had come from the School of Theology? Or, rather, wouldn't the trajectory of this bullet have continued on? Wouldn't it be at the point of entry, the penetration of the bus? And then where would its imaginary bullet track be - or let's say -- let's call it the wound canal - through the bus? How did you determine where the shot had come from if you don't know where it had penetrated the bus and then where it had continued to travel through the bus, what its trajectory there was?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not accept the suggestion that the shot had come from the School of Theology, but I only accepted that if the bus was exposed with the right side to the north-west, that the shot must have originated from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But here it says: [In English] "Alleged shooting position ... Faculty of Theology Nedzarici. Distance to the incident at least 600 metres."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It was not reflected in the transcript. Your report says: "Alleged shooting position is the Faculty of Theology in Nedzarici."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the zone where you determined that the bullet had come in and gone out of the bus? Correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not determine that the bullet went out of the bus. I only read in the victim's statements that first the victim on the right side of the bus was hit and then the other victim -- another victim on the left side of the bus. I did not determine that the bullet came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. But now we have to establish where the shot had come from. You said that it had come from that side. We can agree on that. If the bullet -- if the bus had been struck from the right-hand side, then that's where it was it. But on the right-hand side of the bus you would have an angle of 180 degrees. The possibility would have been that it had come from any of those. So how did you determine that it had come from the School of Theology?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not determine that it came from the School of Theology. That's the alleged shooting position. And the distance to the incident site, because I do not know where the Faculty of Theology actually is, because of the whole area, on page 53 of my paper copy, if you would look at the red field, there is an elliptical shape within -- on the left side within that field of fire. Somewhere within that field I believe the shooter must have been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Then we'll --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- shall we bring up your report, page 53. Because I don't have in colour. E-court number should be different. Fifty-four.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have page 53 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in the meantime, let me ask you this: How did this entry "School of Theology in Nedzarici" find its way into your report if you don't know where that School of Theology is in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this is information given to me by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you then establish where the bullet had come from or was it the OTP?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I established that the bullet must have come from down the street in that -- from that direction, but I did not establish that it had come from the School of Theology since I don't know where that school is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at your report. [In English] "The bullet that wounded the victim first penetrated the bus on the right side, then hit the knee of the victim, hitting at the right side of the bus --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "... and then hit the other victim at the other side of the bus. Since there was a lack of possible shooting position closer than 550 metres, the 7.62x39 millimetres would most probably not have caused the injuries. That round would not have sufficient energy at that range to cause the damage of this incident. That rules out the M-70 series as possible weapon." [Interpretation] So, Mr. Van der Weijden, the bullet penetrated the metal plate of the bus. Then it struck one victim, went through it and struck the second victim. And based on that, you concluded that the bullet had a certain energy; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not the only reason why I ruled out the 7.62x39 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
