utterances.text: You excluded that round because it would not have had sufficient energy; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above 550 metres it would not have sufficient energy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where did you get this 550 metres from? Who suggested this distance to you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have to turn to page -- the next page, page 53, the paper copy. If we could zoom in a little more on the -- the top photograph. Yes. Thank you. As is visible here of the -- of the layout, the buildings lining the street from the incident site to the -- to the green area where I was told by the OTP that during the war screens were put up to -- to blind possible shooters from that direction, if I were to be in a building parallel to -- to the street, I would have to lean out the window to fire at the bus. It would be physically challenging to -- to take a position like that, and it would be very inaccurate. So that's why I concluded that it would most likely -- the shooter would have to be above the 550 metres, and therefore I came to my conclusion that the 7.62x39 millimetres is unlikely to have been used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, would you please explain to the Chamber and to us who is between the green shaded area and the incident site, and why was it not possible for the shot to have been fired from a calibre 7.62 millimetres x 39 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know who exactly is between the green shaded area and the incident site. I was only told that after. But I assume that the screens were put up to -- because beyond that screen there was probably a separation line. But why, it's not possible. I do not -- I cannot completely rule it out, but it would be -- I would have to lean out the window. So I would not -- I could not take a proper shooting position within a room, but I would have to lean out a window. And especially since I would -- I would expose myself to fire. So it's -- it would be very unwise to shoot like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we agree, then, at the spot where it says 550 metres you were told that's where the separation line was; correct? To the west of the screen.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Beyond that, I was not told, but that's -- I was told that beyond that there was -- somewhere, there was a separation line. But I do know -- I do not know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you were told that the origin of fire should be placed in the Serb territory. In other words, to the west of the screen, beyond the 550 metres?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not told that the origin -- origin of fire should be placed. That's what I concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But how did you draw the conclusion to that effect? How did you decide that it wasn't to the east of the green screen and that it was maybe that smaller calibre, the 7.62 x 39 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because if I would be on the south side of that street, I would have to lean out the window and shoot from my left shoulder, which not a lot of people I know are capable of, at least not for a precision shot. And since the bus was parked on the right side, on the northern corner, you would have to float out the window and shoot down the street at the bus. It's physically -- it's almost impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And why would the shots have to be fired from an apartment? Why not from the street to the right of the screen? How did you exclude the entire area of this trajectory, which is 500 metres from the green screen to the bus, how did you conclude that the shooter was in that area? You exclude that.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not mention shots. I only mention one shot fired. And the reason why I excluded the shooter being out in the open on the street is pure logic. It's -- tactically it's not a smart thing to do, and I don't think the bus would be there if there were people shooting on the street. Plus the bus was parked there for a longer time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you account for the fact that this bus was parked full of passengers, that it was not in motion, that it stood in one position for a while? Was there a bus-stop there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. This is something that I had from the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far is the School of Theology from this spot, from the spot that is marked there? Where is the School of Theology here in this photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know what the School of Theology is, nor do I know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it did appear in your report as the alleged origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this was stated in information given to me by the OTP. So as in all incidents, I've put down -- I've written down the alleged shooting position, because that's the -- what I had to work with from the start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So when you began with your work, this was an alleged origin of fire. But once you've completed your report, have you actually established that was actually the origin of fire? In this particular case, did you establish beyond reasonable doubt that the origin of fire was from the -- at the School of Theology, as was suggested to you by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if one were to fire from an -- from anywhere between the green screen and the bus, the shooting would have -- could have been done by a weapon of a smaller calibre; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of a smaller calibre, but it would be a less powered bullet, because it's the same calibre but only with less propellant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it could be a 39 millimetre calibre in this area between the green screen and the bus; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the shooter would be between the green and the incident site, then the distance could be suitable for that cartridge, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, you said earlier on that in order to shoot from that area the shooter must have leaned out from the window. Could you elaborate a bit further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the street -- the street runs parallel to the direction where the shot must -- must have originated from, so the shooter, where normally you would be inside a house and shoot out towards your target, in this case, because the target is parallel to the walls of the buildings, you would have to lean out the window to get a clear view of the incident site. And that would make it very difficult to take a good shooting position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In this picture, you see a, in the middle of that road between that green screen and the bus, that blue part, a rectangular building. From the top of the building, if you have a clean view of that incident, then the shooter did not have to lean out from the window.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to see, because I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's just a hypothetical.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hypothetically, if he would be on a high-rise building, he would be able to see the incident site. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And would you agree that this southern building had some lower buildings and there were some of the windows that are looking out in the direction of the bus? Can you see it? They're not in line completely. Some of them are lower.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some are lower; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What calibre are we talking about, Mr. Van der Weijden? What calibre was involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that if the shooter was above 550, which I think is -- would be tactically -- tactically the more possible solution, then the calibre would be 7.62 x 54R or 7.92 x 57 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But did you know, Mr. Van der Weijden, that the Serb army did not have 7.62 x 54 or 57 but only 7.62 x 39 millimetres? And you actually confirmed this because you saw those invoices where the requisition papers showed that they only had this type of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said it yesterday, I did travel through Sarajevo during the war and I did see, at Serbian checkpoints, weapons that use those two calibres, the 7.92 x 57 and the 7.62 x 54R. So that calibre was available in the Serbian army. I didn't travel through Serbia, but I travelled through Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't have that type of ammunition, but we will prove it in another way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D02410. For the transcript, I said we had ammunition up to 39 millimetres. We did not have 57 and 54. Can we now please have 1D02410.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a photo of the Catholic university, or School of Theology, that was under our control, and we received from one of the friars this photograph. Are you familiar with this building?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that this opening on the narrower side of the building is actually a firing position, that this is how one creates a firing position and with some protection there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that it might be used an as firing position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 2411. 1D02411.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have been allowed to take photos from this opening of the area where the bus was. We were kindly allowed to do that. Now, this is what you could see from there, Mr. Van der Weijden. Would you agree with me that this tree would have taken more than ten years to grow this tall?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude, then, Mr. Van der Weijden, that you only concluded that the bus was struck on the right side and that the shot, the bullet, could have come down that street, and that was the only thing you could conclude, nothing else?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition, I concluded that the bullet was probably of -- of a certain calibre; but for the rest, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender these into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll leave it to Your Honour's discretion. There's nothing in the evidence to support that the location from which this photograph was taken is that as asserted by Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have no objection as to the Faculty of Theology?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No. No -- no objection to that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, can you agree or confirm that this picture or panoramic view is taken from the alleged incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This picture is not taken from the incident site itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Of from the theology, from that opening. You cannot confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know where the School of Theology is, so I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit 1D2410.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D662, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can tender the next -- the 2411 with another witness because this witness cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I with like to take the liberty to ask the Trial Chamber whether they would actually visit the site. And the Defence is willing to provide assistance in the visit to the site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We will consider the matter. Move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, do you recall incident 10 from the F schedule, F10, that is, the incident involving Miljenka Cvitkovica Street, which is presently Ferde Hauptmana Street, and it occurred on 22nd of July, 1994?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly what this incident involved?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation as I was presented involved a 13-year-old boy who was shot and wounded in his belly while he was standing in front of a window with his family on a certain location which is marked in the -- in the several maps, in the photos. I was given the GPS reading. I went to the -- I visited that incident site, checked for possible locations from where a shot might have been fired, and then visited those locations to try to find possible locations where a shooter might have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in the case of this incident, did you -- were you -- did you have -- were you more fortunate in establishing the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not able to pinpoint an exact location, but I was able to -- to determine -- to determine an area where the shot might have come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D02-179.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the old name of this street was Miljenka Cvitkovica, whereas it's now called Ferde Hauptmana? Is that one and the same street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also mentioned in the situation, so I -- I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be helpful when we deal with the map. So what were the principal sources of your information? What did the OTP provide to you in those terms?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the documents that are listed on page 85 of the paper copy, which include an investigation report and some photographs and witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D02192. That's a section of the map of the city of Sarajevo. I apologise, it's 93 -- no. I apologise again. It's 92. It seems that it's time for a break, because I am losing my concentration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much longer do you have with this witness, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Excellency, each of these incidents in any other civilised country would require two or three days of hearing. You can see how I am tackling each of these incidents very superficially by relying on the -- that many of them are contained in the adjudicated facts. I leave it to the Trial Chamber's discretion to decide about that, but if we're allowed, we may file a complaint in that sense. But as I said, this witness is extremely helpful, and we really need to establish what was done in a wrong way. Please accept my apology. I'm not criticising the previous Trial Chambers, but the differences between legal systems created such a situation. So therefore, I would like to -- you to allow me to go through each and every incident or to have the whole F list of incidents rejected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you didn't indicate how much longer you would need to complete your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, we have covered only one-third of the incidents. We shed at least some light on them. So allow me to confer with my team, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have gone through half of the incidents. What remains are some minor incidents, and they won't take so much time. We've gone through the minor -- to the more serious incidents such as the Marin Dvor, et cetera. Therefore, I would require two to three [as interpreted] sessions to complete this in a satisfactory way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break now for half an hour. So when we resume at 25 minutes past 12.00, we'll let you know how much you have or how you should proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please correct the record. I said three to four sessions and not two to three. It seems that I have been sabotaged or undermined by the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber considered the cross-examination of Mr. Karadzic so far. While the lines of questions cannot be said to be irrelevant, in some cases the questions were repetitive, and overall I don't think it's a very efficient conduct of cross-examination and there should be ways to conduct more efficiently. So the Chamber is telling you, Mr. Karadzic, given that we had -- we had experienced technical difficulties in bringing up maps, et cetera, so we'll give you another session today. So try to finish your

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That said, shall we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned, there's no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: During the cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic raised the issue of on-site visit by the Trial Chamber to the places. The Chamber is minded to hear the views of the parties in relation to that issue. And then at the end of day, the Chamber need a written motion from the parties. But before that, at the end of the next conclusion of the evidence of next witness, I'll invite the parties to address the Chamber orally. Let's go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With the highest regard, I would kindly ask you to understand the Defence position, and that is that we shall deem covered and examined only those incidents that we were able to examine. As for the remainder, we cannot consider them to be examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, are you familiar with this map? It is related to F incident number 10.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise features of the map, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Can you mark the site of the incident F10 that you investigated?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since it's not a topographical map, I can only indicate an area, but it would -- it would be within this area.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: But you encircled the Zmaja od Bosne Street, whereas the incident took place on the Miljenka Cvitkovica Street which is now called the Ferde Hauptmana Street. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this map, this street is marked Zmaja od Bosne; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Can you mark the Miljenka Cvitkovica or the Ferde Hauptmana Street, which is, in fact, the incident site.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not see it on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Do you have a map of your own that you used in your report? How did you make these markings in your report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made the markings with the GPS reading of the victim location together with the area of photography and the terrain features.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Well, how shall we find our bearings in this map? Will this map, which is at the same time the map of the city and the topographic map, be of help to you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The topographical map might be of help. But this is not a topographical map.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: May I kindly ask you to take this American map and to show us -- [In English] This is this section. This section.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it might save a lot of time if we simply use 65 ter 13578, which shows the incident site marked on it. And then the witness can be questioned as to whether he agrees with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. Let's try that first. 13578.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Is it now easier, Mr. Van der Weijden? And can we say that the Ferde Hauptmana Street is the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this map, the Ferde Hauptmana appears to be north of the location of the incident.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: But in all the documents it is stated that the incident took place and Miljenka Cvitkovica Street which has been renamed Ferde Hauptmana. How did that happen? How did -- how was the incident site moved to the south?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Did you work on the assumption that the incident happened on Miljenka Cvitkovica Street as stated in all the documents produced by the Bosnian police, or was your working assumption a completely different one?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not just the street location as a marking because I used the photographical -- of the photos from the evidence, which show the window of the shop that is still there as the location for the incident site. I didn't look into the exact name of the street where the incident was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we move on, Mr. Gaynor, this map we are looking at now is map 12 of the binder, but those markings are done by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, based on GPS readings obtained by an OTP investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then that red 10 refers to the sniping incident F10?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be helpful if the OTP would clarify to us how it happened that this building is positioned with regard to Ferde Hauptmana Street. Maybe Mr. Van der Weijden also can help us, but in all the documents we have the address of the incident site as Miljenka Cvitkovica Street number 4. It is now called, as I said, Ferde Hauptmana Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is for the parties. Ferde Hauptmana Street is the one which runs from north to south, between Nedima Filipovica and Zmaja od Bosne?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that the street goes in a square. And to the north of the row of shops marked with the red dot is also part of the street, and the incident happened on the south side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Defence team visited the location, and we are going to present that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Now, what was your conclusion as regards the origin of the shot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the evidence from the report including the round retrieved on -- from the restaurant, that already indicates that the shot might -- must have come from the general direction of the south. With my -- with myself at the exact location, I viewed towards the south and determined what buildings would have a view, a direct view, on the incident site, and with -- thereby and with eliminating tactical or tactical impossibilities or unlikely situations, I came out -- I came up on the fields of fire as I've marked on page 80 of my report.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Can we now look at 65 ter 0965T, which is actually Exhibit P19, page 11. In the meantime, let me ask you this, Mr. Van der Weijden --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we admit this map with markings --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The markings were made by the OTP. However, I would like Mr. Van der Weijden to mark the direction and the place where he was and how he reached his conclusion with regard to the spot of the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Can you please use the pen.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be the approximate location. It's where I -- from where I took my measurements and the general direction, and from there I viewed the wide area, and I came up with the markings as are visible on page 80 of the report. By -- the buildings on the -- on this map, only the high-rise buildings are visible, so it's -- it's not possible for me to draw the fields of fire on this -- the basis of this map, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: But we do agree, don't we, that the possible shot came from the 50 or the 55 angles that you have marked here. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, what 50 or 55 angles?

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: You have drawn the range within which you think the bullet could have come on. I'm talking about degrees, not bullets. Your drawing is a bit more than 90 degrees. One hundred and eighty degree is to the south, and your markings indicate 90 to 100 degrees. Is that the range or the area within which or from which the shot could have come?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These two -- two lines that I have drawn just now, they represent the area from which I started. So they didn't -- they don't represent the area where I think the shots have originated from, but this is where I started from, and from there I went on eliminating areas.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: What prompted you to apply this range? Or more precisely, did you take the bullet path at the incident site into consideration or as a predominant factor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did take it into consideration as a general direction but not for the extreme or the precise direction.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: But why did you start with such a wide area? What was your motive for doing that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the shots did not originate from within the shop. So that's why I started with the -- the whole area to the south.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: But what was the decisive factor for you taking such a broad area? Were you guided by the bullet path at the incident site, and did that give you an idea that it might have come from this particular area? Why didn't you start with a broader or a maybe narrower area?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I wanted to keep all possibilities open.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us where the bullet was fired from? But first of all, tell me what were the consequences of the shot? What did the bullet produce?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one bullet retrieved from the wall in the restaurant, so inside, and there was -- from the hole in the window, in conjunction with the hole in the -- the impact on the wall, that gives -- that gives back -- further points back to a certain location. From my experience with shooting through glass, glass has a big effect on the path of the bullet. So the line from the impact in the wall through the glass doesn't necessarily exactly lead back to the location of the shooter. So that's how I narrowed down my field -- the area.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. What kind of the angle of refraction are we talking when we have glass in the path of the bullet? We know how the water surface reflect -- refracts, but can you tell me something about the angle and how this angle is affected if glass is in the way of a shot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would depend on the type of window. If the window is a loose pain of glass or if it's within a frame, if it's single -- a single layer or a double-layered glass, if it's tempered glass, if it's safety glass. So it depends on the type of glass that is used for the window. But in general, when a bullet hits the glass at an angle, it will turn inwards. So it does -- will not ricochet, as most people would expect, but because the bullet -- the side of the bullet that is closest to the window meets the first resistance of the window, it will cause the bullet to turn more inwards. I would have to -- I could draw it out if that would make it clearer.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Unfortunately we don't have time for that, but we can all imagine that the path is deflecting just as it happens when an object is going from the air into water. So you had two points, a hole in the wall and a hole in the window or in the glass. If you were to extend this line, how would you then conclude the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this was done by the investigator at the time of the incident or at the -- later on that day, and they came to -- I believe they came to an origin of fire that was slightly east of the area that I concluded. But I would like to rectify that the path is not deflecting. It's towards the other -- it's -- the bullet comes through the other side. So it doesn't ricochet on glass.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: But it doesn't travel along the straight line. Once it passes through the glass, it changes its direction. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There can be -- in general, there's a slight change in direction. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Is that done to such an extent that it has to be taken into consideration in determining the origin of fire, or is it not relevant enough and can be disregarded?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not disregard it.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Which coefficient did you apply in adjusting or correcting the path? In this particular case.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I did not know exactly which kind of 7.62 bullet was used, I cannot determine which coefficient -- ballistic coefficient the bullet has.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Was the bullet ever found? It was found in the wall, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bullet that was found in the wall, that was retrieved and was written about at least in the investigation report.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Was this bullet shown to you or were you given a photograph of it with its characteristics?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given a photograph, but the only characteristics was that it states that it was a 7.62-millimetre bullet.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: What was the size of the bullet, 39, 54?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the bullet -- the 39 and 54 don't refer to the bullet itself. They refer to the length of the casing.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: But what was the casing of the bullet that was fired?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would not be at the incident site. It would be at the location of the shooter.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: All right. So what were the consequences of that shot? And I'm sorry for trying to be as quick as possible. You didn't say anything about the consequences. Was there a boy who was wounded in that incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the situation that I received from OTP, there was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 09652. That's P19 -- or my apologies. Before that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Witness, would you please just put the date and your initials on this. And could you mark the map to show the direction from which the round had come. You have marked here the range, but could you also indicate the range of the possible directions from which the bullet may have come.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we change the colour of this. So far we used blue, and then we'll use black for the possible direction of the fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could we erase that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: The witness needs help, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Please, could you rehabilitate this part of blue and then do in black.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd just like to note, Mr. President, the witness is being asked to reproduce exactly the same information which appears on page 80 of his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I don't know if it's a complete waste of time to undertake this exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is not a topographical map, so it wouldn't -- it's only an indication.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Excellency, you would have been able to see that according to 92 ter Rule whether this was useful for the Defence or not, but I accept your suggestion. Can we admit this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: But before that, can you explain these four lines? Are all four of them important, or are only two of them important?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will mark them like this so they will be similar to the fields of fire in my report. So all four lines were important, because between the two lines on the left, that's an area that offers a view of the incident site, and the same goes for the two right lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us move on. Again, this was a repetition of this witness's report. Yes, we'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D663.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, do you like to tender the exhibit which reflects the changes of the street name, or it won't be necessary because it was confirmed that the Ferde Hauptmana Street is the current name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do not have to burden the evidence if we all agree that this is reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, why wasn't it possible for a shot to come between these two fields that you indicated? Why wasn't it possible for a bullet to come between these two cones?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I excluded that building because of logical reasoning. There were -- there was a big group of people present on and around the incident site, and they would not be present if there was firing from that building because that building was very close to the incident site.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: And why, then, would it not have been possible for the shot to have come from one -- from the hill there, from some part of that area? What was it that prevented you from concluding that this entire area could actually be the area from which it could have come? So if we can just go back a little. Was there anything in between these two cones? Was there anything obstructing this line from the bases of the two cones?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the earlier document on the screen D663. We're have not -- we're not done with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Karadzic, the witness answered the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the question wasn't clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Now, these two cones, why was it that they could have been the trajectory of the bullet, whereas the area in between could not? We don't have a clear answer to that.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area in between the two cones is blocked by a high-rise building close to the location of the incident site, and as I explained, this is -- for logical reasons, I did exclude that building. So that would leave -- that would make a gap between the two cones. It's not visible on the map because it's -- the map is not precise enough for me to draw the lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you can mark the location of that high-rise building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I've -- it's impossible for me to work with this map because the aerial photographs or the pictures on the ground, that I've taken on the ground, should be -- should give enough visual insight, especially the pictures on -- of the photos on page 82 of my paper report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Now, what kind of logic -- logical thinking did you apply to conclude that the shots could not have come between -- from between these two -- somewhere between these two buildings? Why was -- why did you come to that conclusion? In other words, Mr. Van der Weijden, were these two cones, in fact, attempts to locate Serb positions and not all the possible sites from which the fire would have originated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is, again, an answered question. Witness said he excluded the building because of logical reasoning, which is reflected in line 1 to 4 on page 65.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, his answer was not satisfactory, because this was actually trying to nudge this a bit so that it would indicate to a Serb position. Now, could we please look again at 09652.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, do you like to add something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I -- as I've -- as you have explained before, the reason why I came to my conclusion, because it's the same as I've written on page 83 of my paper copy in identification, in the witness statements that there were people, up to ten people, present in the restaurant and also on the terrace of the restaurant. There were children playing. And this would be very unlikely if fighting had been going on nearby. And that includes the first -- the high-rise building that separates the two cones. So I do not -- I cannot completely exclude it, but I -- it doesn't make sense if people are on the street enjoining a meal if -- if the possibility of shooting from close by exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's better.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can now remove this. And if we can have 65 ter 09652, please. P19. Maybe that's going to be easier to locate. Page 1. Yes, in B/C/S we have the right document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been a long time since I've looked at these documents, but I do recognise some names, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Did this investigation produce any results about a young boy being wounded in Miljenka Cvitkovica Street number 4?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we slide, please, to -- the left page to the top of the page. Thank you. And could we switch to the previous page for this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it this is the first page, but why don't we show the witness only the B/C/S and the coloured pictures. Show the second page, third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: If we can only agree that this is in fact Miljenka Cvitkovica Street number 4 and that on page 1 we saw that the Bosnian police indicated that it was an incident at Miljenka Cvitkovica number 4; correct? We see it here too. Do you agree with me that in the second line it says Miljenka Cvitkovica Street --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's show him the English page as well. Second page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't -- as I read this, it is number 4. But I only checked with the GSP co-ordinate and the incident as pointed out to me by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I will have now to intervene in the translation. This shop is a wide view of the scene, and the cafe - and I would appreciate the interpreters checking what I'm reading - owned by Mehmed Mujanovic at -- in Miljenka Cvitkovica Street behind number 4, which is not what it says in English, because in English it says at number 4, which was exposed to sniper fire from aggressor position on July 22nd, 1994, and on that occasion a boy named Seid Solak was injured in the vicinity. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the other language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your reading was translated. Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that we see this is an outdoor cafe, Arijana cafe, and that this is open to patrons? The cafe's open; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps the accused can move on a bit. If he wants to submit this file of photographs, we certainly won't object. The kind of question he's just asked right now is really quite obvious to anyone looking at the photographs. Perhaps he can move on to his point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And he doesn't need to tender it because it has been already admitted. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I will now have to disclose my case. This is Dzemala Bijedica Street, and Miljenka Cvitkovica is behind it. And the entire confusion and the inconsistency actually arises from these details. And this is not the only case. In other cases, too, that kind of confusion was evident. And what I would now like to see is to see what Mirsad Kucanin said in his report. He's the person who conducted the investigation between 10 and 12 November 1995. That's 09939 or, rather, Exhibit P23, page 2. Can we please pull that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, Mr. Van der Weijden, are you familiar with the term "Kuca Przulja"?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the next page, please. And another one, please. The next one -- or, rather, we need page 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: And it said in the first line: "From Zagorska Street -- or, rather, from the Przulja house there was a lot of shooting and the BH Army had under its control through the entire period of the war of this area." Now, did you have occasion to see this report by the Sarajevo police? And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The army of Bosnian Serbs, not the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: And to assist you further, this is a statement that an investigator of the Sarajevo police gave to the OTP, and what does he say on? In the file there's photo number 8, which shows the house called Przulja. The shots were doubtlessly fired from that position. And then he goes on to say, I don't know what the results of the ballistic investigation was -- were because each individual is in charge of his own field of expertise and area of responsibility and so on and so forth. Now, were you able to establish that the shot had come from the Przulja house, or, rather, did you actually establish where the shot had originated?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not establish if the shot had come from the Przulja house because when I visited the site there was a new building obstructing the view from the house pointed out in the photograph to the incident site, so I was not able to see Przulja house because of the new building. And for -- I did not indicate a single location from where I believe the shot originated from. I only indicated an area.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: In other words, we do not know the exact place, the exact origin of fire, and we cannot say or state that it was at Przulja -- from Przulja house; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a moment. Please bear with me while I confer with my team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: I just have one more question, Mr. Van der Weijden. Were you told by anyone that the incident site as arises from the documentation of the Bosnian police is actually recorded as a site behind this cafe and that they actually used the street of Miljenka Cvitkovica instead of Dzemala Bijedica, that was a confusion on the two streets?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: From the northern side. I don't know what it states in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe we're done with this incident. We can now move on. Mr. Van der Weijden, do you remember the incident of 18th November 1994 that you also worked on, involving the wounding of Dzenana Sokolovic and the death of her son Nermin Divovic who was killed on the occasion? That is F4, incident F4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think Mr. Karadzic probably means incident F12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Page 81 of your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I recall, an incident involving those two people in case number 12 on page 91 of my paper copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ninety-one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: You're right. I apologise. It is incident F12 of November 18. Now we have to go back to Marin Dvor, the same location at Franjo Racki Street. Could you please tell us briefly what this incident entailed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In incident number 12 or F12, a mother and her son are walking -- and her daughter are walking home. They were -- on the intersection they were shot and her son was -- was fatally wounded, and she was wounded in her stomach. And from the information source, the alleged shooting position is Grbavica, or the area, and there was an international firefighter who assisted at the scene and made a photographic record of the incident.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you do research of -- on this incident in the -- in General Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Did you establish that the shot was fired from the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Metalka building is the same building as I've marked in the layouts, then it would be the same building.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you establish that it was fired from there or that it could have been fired from there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I established that it most likely had been fired from there.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: And how many other places were -- were there from which the shots were less likely to have come from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- the shooter could have been on the street, in the middle of the street. And that were the only possibilities, the further possibilities.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of the contradictions involving the incident site where they were hit, that Dzenana Sokolovic herself said in one of her statements that she was hit before she actually stepped onto the pedestrian crossing, and then in her other statement she said that it was on the pedestrian crossing? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Is it your position that the bullet had first passed through the abdomen of the mother and then hit her son in the head, passed through her and hit her son in the head?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the information that was given to me by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Were you told that the medical records indicate -- or stated that, that was one version, and then the other version in the medical records was that the bullet had first actually hit the child and then passed through him and hit the mother?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Do you know what the entry and exit wounds were and where they were on the body of Dzenana Sokolovic? You can use your notes if you need to refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Were you told that in one version the conclusion was that the bullet had entered through the left side and then exited on the right side and that later on that was actually reversed, and it was concluded that the bullet had come in from the right and exited through the left? We have all that medical -- all those medical records. Have you been shown them, these records?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's take a look at General Milosevic's judgement and see what it has to say about this incident. That's paragraphs 325 and on. At 329 it says the following: "Lieutenant Van der Weijden --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you don't need to rely on judgement by the other Chamber. Just put your case or -- or if you would like to refer to the evidence given by this witness, you may do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Well, what I'm trying to say is that in the judgement itself it was established that there was complete confusion in this matter. For instance, were you told that the wounds were practically parallel, the entry and exit wounds, that they were at the same height; and this was something that Dr. Sefik Beslic established?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall that.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Would -- if a shot was fired from the street, would the wounds be parallel, the entry and exit wound?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a shot was fired from down the street, the wounds would not be parallel, but there would be a wound channel parallel to the street. It would be a wound channel instead of a wound in general.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: And the entry and exit wounds would be approximately at the same height; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: In respect of the ground. Now, if a shot was fired from a tall building, would it have the same result or with it be different?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would depend from where within the tall building the shot would be fired.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: According to your findings, was it possible to fire from the Metalka building from any level, or did it have to come from the 8th floor in view of the trees that were there and also the position of the building in respect of the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were possible shooting positions throughout the building on all levels, only differing in -- in views. One view would be more than from another position.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: From which position would it have been better?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position that I visited or the apartment which I visited was on the 4th floor, and on the 4th -- because -- I visited that apartment because there are bullet holes around the windows. So I assume that had been -- that had been a shooting position and had been return fired upon. And from that position, I was -- I took the photograph toward the incident site. So that has been my -- that was on the right side of the building, the eastern side of the building. So not the east side but the eastern side, facing north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, you identified some certain scope of those windows that would offer the view on the incident on page 8 -- 93 in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I did. I checked the building. I was not able to go into all the apartments, of course, but on all -- on several levels in the staircase I checked for views of the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: And which position offers the best view of the intersection or the Sniper Alley, from which particular floor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not establish that because I was not able to visit all the apartments.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Have you established exactly where the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we please have this intersection with the Sniper Alley on our screens. Can I have a moment, please. 65 ter 21216. Can we zoom in on the intersection in the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, have you seen Dzenana Sokolovic's statement in which she said that the shot was fired before she stepped on the zebra with her children? This is what she said in her original statement. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be right. I would have to re-read it.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: And the original medical report said that the entry wound was on the left. Do you agree that she was facing east -- or, rather, that she was coming from the museum towards the Faculty of Philosophy?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The travel direction would be from west to east. I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: So from west to east. And she was closer to the museum on the pavement when she was hit. Do you agree that if the entry wound is on the left-hand side, she must have been shot at from the position where the photograph -- photographer is standing, that is, close to the Holiday Inn Hotel?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I agree then, she would have -- if the entry wound would have been on the left side, then she would have to be fired upon from the north to the south.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you. So her original statement says that she was not on the zebra crossing yet and that the wound was on the left-hand side. What followed, Mr. Van der Weijden, after the wound healed, a new opinion emerged by Dr. Beslic stating that the entry wound was on the right-hand side, after all, and that the exit wound was on the left. And he concluded that by measuring the size of the scar. In your experience, is it possible to take the size of the scar to determine where the bullet entered and exited, because this does not affect -- the scar only indicates how the healing process went on.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my general knowledge, I would -- the entry wound is usually smaller than an exit wound, but I do not know the amount of surgery and extra scars that would have formed after she was treated in hospital.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Let me just remind you of the original medical report saying that the entry wound was on the right and exit was on the left. After the wound healed, Dr. Beslic is trying, based on the size of the scar, to arrive at a different conclusion. If the wound is infected in the healing process, would the scar be larger in that case?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it for the witness to answer those questions, Mr. Karadzic? You don't have to put everything to the witness. Put questions to which the witness is able to answer and to which he dealt with.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, this witness worked on the same case. He must have been shown all the relevant documents on the basis of which he would have been able to draw conclusions. If something was concealed from him or not shown to him, then we must wonder how we proceed. The original findings were as I described them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Do you know what the medical records and what the doctor said from day one relating to this incident, and did you take them into consideration when drawing your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall, since I have in longer access to those medical records.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: May I ask you to mark the place on the pavement from which one stepped onto the pedestrian crossing on Franjo Racki Street.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does the Chamber need this, or what we have in the transcript sufficient?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can move. We can do without.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, do you believe that this spot where these three casualties took place is important for the shooter to aim at this particular spot if he is located in the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which spot, the zebra crossing?

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: No, no. As stated in the original statement, it was said that it happened before they stepped on the zebra crossing, that they were wounded on the pavement. Do you think that is relevant and important?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: So the shooter would have had a very short time to aim; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE END OF TODAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can't go on. I think that we have examined this incident enough. We have to go through other incidents as well. I would kindly ask the Chamber to give me two or three sessions. So that would be very important for the dignity of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you have had almost six hours and half an hour, two hours and a half in excess of the original time given to you. It is for you to plan how to cross-examine the witness. If there's -- if there remains some place which you couldn't cover, it is -- it is your responsibility. Tomorrow you will have a half an hour to conclude. That will be it. But tomorrow we'll be sitting in the afternoon, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, this is 13 and a half hours less than what I requested for this witness, so I was allocated only one-third of the time that I asked for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is our final ruling, Mr. Karadzic. Otherwise, we can go forever if you wish. Half an hour tomorrow. 2.15 tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
